sourcedFrom: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) (2022)
cleanIntro: Iver Johnson's own 1911 book covers eight models under one cover, and it prints two different strip procedures. The 1911A1 — the 5-inch, GI-sighted gun in the model table — takes the standard bushing-and-plug strip on pages 35 to 41. The Thrasher is the one model in the line that does not, and the manual says which pages are whose.

steps.title: One book, two strips — check which pages are yours
steps.action: Iver Johnson prints two disassembly procedures in this manual and tells you which to read. The model table on page 4 lists the 1911A1 as the 5-inch gun with GI-style sights in .45 ACP or 9mm. If that is your pistol, the procedure below is yours and pages 42 to 48 — the Thrasher's — do not apply to it.
steps.aside: no barrel bushing on the Thrasher
steps.quote: (If you do not have the model Thrasher, read the entire manual except for pages 42-48)
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Glossary, p.3
steps.warn: The Thrasher has no barrel bushing at all, and a bushing is the first thing the procedure below asks you to rotate. Running these steps on a Thrasher means turning a part that is not there.

steps.title: Iver Johnson bars +P and reloaded ammunition in this pistol
steps.action: Worth knowing before the gun goes back together and out to the range: the maker prohibits +P in this line, with one exception it names itself, and prohibits reloads outright. This is a warranty condition printed on the cover as well as in the body, not general advice.
steps.quote: Never use +P ammunition, unless firing a 38super pistol, or any type of reloaded ammunition with this firearm.
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Safety notices, p.5

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked with the slide locked open
steps.action: Drop the magazine, lock the slide back and put your eye into the chamber area of the barrel. Lock it open first rather than checking through a closed action — a 1911's ejection port hides a case rim from one angle or another depending on how you hold it, and a locked-back slide removes the argument.
steps.caution: The springs in the gun are strong and could cause items to fly out, which could injure your eyes.
steps.quote: Ensure the magazine is removed and the gun is unloaded by visually checking the chamber area of the barrel with the slide locked open (Figure 8).
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly, step 1, p.35
steps.warn: This pistol has no magazine disconnect. The manual states on p.33 that it will fire with no magazine in it, so dropping the magazine is not the same as clearing the gun.

steps.title: Butt on the bench, plug pressed, bushing turned clockwise
steps.action: Stand the pistol on its butt with the muzzle up and press the recoil spring plug down, just under the barrel muzzle. Holding it down, rotate the barrel bushing clockwise about a quarter turn — Iver Johnson recommends a 1911 bushing wrench for this. The plug is under full recoil spring load the entire time your thumb is on it.
steps.aside: With the muzzle pointing upwards, rest the butt of the gun on a work bench.
steps.quote: Press down on the recoil spring plug, just under the barrel muzzle, and while pressing down, turn the barrel bushing clockwise about a 1/4” turn, as in figure 9
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly, step 3, p.36

steps.title: Plug and spring let down under control
steps.action: Once the bushing is clear of the plug, do not simply lift your thumb. Keep the pressure on and bleed the tension off gradually until the spring is fully relaxed, then take the plug off. This is the single step in a 1911 strip that most often loses a part into the carpet.
steps.quote: AT THIS TIME, THE RECOIL SPRING CAN FLY OUT. Keep pressure on the recoil spring plug, and gradually release it until all tension is gone (Figure 7).
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly warning, p.37
steps.warn: Wear eye protection for this step. The manual asks for safety glasses through the whole disassembly and this is why.

steps.title: Hammer cocked, disassembly notch aligned, slide stop out
steps.action: Cock the hammer first — with it down the slide will not sit where it needs to. Draw the slide back until the disassembly notch in its lower edge lines up with the lug on the slide stop, then push the slide stop's shaft in from the right side of the frame and draw the stop out to the left. If it resists, the notch has drifted off; reset the slide rather than levering the stop.
steps.aside: Remove the slide stop pin by pushing the slide stop pin from the right side of the frame, in Figure 10, and pulling the slide stop out from the left side of the frame, in Figure 11.
steps.quote: Cock the hammer. Pull the slide back until the disassembly notch, page 23, is directly in line with the lug on the slide stop.
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly, step 4, p.37

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, then the recoil guide and spring
steps.action: Run the slide forward along the rails and off the front of the frame — barrel, bushing and recoil assembly all travel with it, so support the weight as it leaves. Then take the recoil guide rod and spring out of the slide.
steps.aside: Remove the recoil guide rod and spring
steps.quote: Once the pin is removed, remove the slide by sliding it forward off the gun (Figure 12).
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly, step 5, p.38

steps.title: Bushing back the other way, barrel out the front
steps.action: Rotate the barrel bushing counter-clockwise until it stops — about an eighth of a turn past centre — then draw the barrel forward out of the front of the slide, bringing the bushing with it. Flip the barrel link fully forward first, or the link catches on the way out and the barrel will not clear.
steps.prose: Make sure the barrel link is fully forward so it fits out the front of the slide (Figure 14).
steps.aside: Then slide the barrel forward and off the front of the slide.
steps.quote: Turn the barrel bushing counter-clockwise until it stops, which should be about 1/8th of a turn past center.
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly, step 7, p.39

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel, bushing, recoil spring, guide rod and plug are off the frame. That is the whole strip Iver Johnson publishes for this pistol, and the book closes the section by saying so. The parts illustration later in the manual is for identifying components, not a teardown sheet.
steps.quote: Do not strip your pistol any further than we have noted here. This is the only stripping necessary for cleaning your pistol.
steps.cite: Manual for 1911 style Pistols & Carbines — 1-1-22 (printed on the back cover) — Cleaning your Firearm, Disassembly, p.39

deepAbsentReason: Iver Johnson's 1911 book publishes the seven-step field strip on pages 35 to 39 and then closes it in its own words: no further stripping is necessary for cleaning, and anything beyond it goes to a licensed gunsmith. The 1911 parts illustration on pages 51 and 52 states on its own face that it is only a reference for identifying parts. There is no firing pin, extractor, mainspring housing or fire-control procedure anywhere in the fifty-eight pages, so no deeper procedure was invented from it.

cleaning.name: BORE, SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Run gun solvent through the barrel, then through the inside of the slide and the frame
Clean well into the rails of both the slide and the frame — that is where a tight 1911 collects grit
Wipe the breech face and under the extractor claw
Once the solvent is off, put gun oil on the slide and frame rails

cleaning.name: BARREL, RECOIL PARTS & INTERNALS
tasks: Wipe the barrel exterior, the lugs, the link and the feed ramp
Wipe the recoil spring, guide rod, plug and the bushing's inner face where the barrel rides
Apply a light coat of oil to any visible internal parts
Do not oil or grease ammunition — the manual warns it can damage the primer

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & INTERVAL
tasks: Keep the magazine body and follower free of grit; the pistol ships with an empty magazine for service returns
Clean the pistol after every use, and as soon as possible if it gets wet
If it is not being used, clean it at least twice a year and keep it well oiled

reassembly: To reassemble the firearm, reverse the disassembly instructions.
Fit the barrel into the slide from the front with the link forward, then the bushing, rotating it back to lock.
Return the recoil spring and guide rod, then run the slide onto the frame rails.

Before the slide stop goes in, line the barrel link up with the slide stop pin hole so the pin passes through the frame and the link both — forcing it with the link out of line is how a link gets bent.
Compress the recoil spring plug under your thumb and rotate the bushing back over it to capture it.
fncheck: With no magazine in the pistol, pull the slide fully back and release it; it should run forward over the empty chamber and leave the hammer cocked. Then prove both safeties: with the hammer cocked and the thumb safety up the trigger must not drop it, and with the safety off it must. Finally insert an empty magazine, cycle the slide, confirm it locks open, and confirm the firing pin is not standing proud of its hole in the breech face.
